minutes.headline: Conservation Commission workshopped special conditions for the Lake Shirley management NOI; no vote was taken.
minutes.summary: The commission held a workshop on the Lake Shirley Improvement Corps' Notice of Intent for aquatic plant and algae management. Topics were species loss data, fish kill reporting, drawdown depth, herbicide pretreatment surveys, algae monitoring dates, the annual report and peer review. Members and the consultants disagreed at times over oversight of the applicator. Draft conditions are to be updated and circulated; no formal vote was recorded.

public_comment.topic: A lake association speaker said the Lake Shirley Improvement Corps has worked with the commission since 2006 without blocking the consultant's treatment decisions, and that people are tired of the conversation.

budget_items.topic: Low-dose alum and retention pond maintenance
budget_items.what_was_said: A quote was mentioned for a low-dose treatment, plus yearly upkeep for a retention pond.
Grants would require a municipality to apply and a local match would likely come from the town.
A speaker said the association pays for the consultant's decisions each year.

decisions.decision: Members agreed to add a special condition on reporting fish kills, modeled on an example order, with contact to Fish and Game.
Consensus that the drawdown condition would allow up to six feet, with variation left to weather and results; the specific depth was to be confirmed in writing with the agency.
Agreed to use a May-1st-or-earlier start for clarity readings, with a parenthetical allowing weather adjustment, and to bring the water quality monitoring paragraph into the special conditions.
Annual report to cover one drawdown cycle (fall to fall) with a hard due date, and no repeat alternatives review every three years.
The consultant will update the draft conditions next week and send them to commissioners.
With no quorum, the warrant article would be submitted before the deadline and ratified later.

what_happened.line: The Conservation Commission held a workshop on special conditions for the Lake Shirley Improvement Corps' aquatic plant and algae management Notice of Intent; no vote was taken.
Members agreed to add a special condition requiring fish kill reporting, with contact to Fish and Game, modeled on an example order.
Consensus held that the drawdown condition would allow up to six feet, with variation left to weather and results, and the depth to be confirmed in writing with the agency.
Members agreed the annual report would cover one drawdown cycle with a hard due date, and that no repeat alternatives review would be required every three years.
Oversight of herbicide pretreatment surveys and the applicator drew disagreement between members and consultants, and was not resolved.

why_it_matters: The special conditions set what the lake group must monitor, report and justify when managing weeds and algae in Lake Shirley, which affects the lake's condition and what the association pays for consultants and treatment.
Watershed grants and any alum treatment would need a municipality to apply and likely provide a local match, which could become a request on the town budget, mostly taxes.
watch_next: The consultant's updated draft conditions, due to be sent to commissioners the week after the meeting.
The warrant article, to be submitted before the deadline and ratified later because the commission lacked a quorum.
